suites.title: Proposing what kind of document a source is

sets.description: Short synthetic documents, four or five per kind in the default cue pack plus four that should get no kind. Labelled by hand when the set was written (UW-13); file names carry no cue, so only the content decides.

measures.title: Right kind proposed first
No kind proposed when none applies
Certificate precision
Certificate recall

limits: A small synthetic set written with the cue pack in view; it shows the mechanism works, not how it does on real documents.
Kinds are proposals for a person to confirm, never decisions; this measures the proposal only.

suites.title: Finding protected values before a model request leaves

sets.description: An invented client register (16 values) and 66 labelled texts: known values exact and varied (misspelt, transliterated, initials, reordered, in file names, look-alike letters, base64 and percent-encoding), Indian identifiers with valid check digits, and 20 texts that must not be blocked.

measures.title: Exact known values blocked
Texts carrying a protected value that were caught
Entities found that were really there
Clean texts that would have been blocked

notes: By form: exact 11/11, case 2/2, misspelt 4/4, transliterated 3/3, initials 2/2, reordered 1/1, file-name 3/3, look-alike 2/2, encoded 3/3, nickname 0/1, spelt-out 0/1, identifier 13/13.
Entity-level: 45 found correctly, 0 extra, 2 not found.
limits: Synthetic and small: it shows which forms the detectors handle, not their rate on real customer text. Measuring on real (consented, local) data is an owner decision.
Written by the engineer who wrote the detectors, so it is not blind (compare ADR 0030): a held-out set written by someone else is needed before a threshold is ratified.
Names that are in no spreadsheet and no setting are not detected: that needs the NER sidecar (14c-3), deferred until a vertical must send free text.
Transliteration coverage is a fixed spelling key (ksh/x, aspirates, sh/s, w/v, z/j, doubled letters, vowel runs), not a learned model.

suites.title: Reading real documents XO was not written against

sets.description: Fourteen public-domain / CC0 documents by US federal teams (18F, CISA, USDS), each in the formats it travels in (original Word, Markdown or PDF; web page; Word; PDF export; Word HTML export; printed-and-scanned PDF). Every sentence or list item is labelled with its expected reading under a written policy. Three splits: dev (used to find and fix failures), held-out (labelled before XO ran on it; its failures were seen once, at the baseline, and never used to tune), and blind (labelled before any fix and measured once, at the end).

notes: blind by format: Markdown: 18/21 items read right, 18/28 outputs right; Word: 29/34 items read right, 29/43 outputs right; scanned PDF: 16/21 items read right, 16/25 outputs right; web page: 20/27 items read right, 20/27 outputs right; PDF: 22/29 items read right, 22/34 outputs right; Word HTML export: 9/11 items read right, 9/11 outputs right.
blind failure modes: missed-silently 7, missed-reported 22, spurious-from-non-content 9, unmatched-output 42.

held-out by format: Word: 56/62 items read right, 57/68 outputs right; PDF: 23/37 items read right, 24/35 outputs right; scanned PDF: 12/20 items read right, 12/15 outputs right; Markdown: 46/52 items read right, 47/56 outputs right; web page: 36/42 items read right, 37/45 outputs right; Word HTML export: 10/10 items read right, 10/11 outputs right.
held-out failure modes: missed-silently 32, missed-reported 7, wrong-kind 1, duplicate 4, spurious-from-non-content 13, unmatched-output 29.

dev by format: Word: 46/46 items read right, 46/48 outputs right; PDF: 13/13 items read right, 13/14 outputs right; scanned PDF: 22/24 items read right, 22/23 outputs right; Markdown: 39/39 items read right, 39/39 outputs right; web page: 39/39 items read right, 39/39 outputs right.
limits: Fourteen documents from three US federal teams, all English and all about software delivery or administration. They are real, but they are not a customer's documents; the pilot set is still owed (R12).
Labels are one reader's reading under a written policy; ambiguous text is labelled neutral rather than forced either way.

Format variants other than the originals were produced by pandoc and LibreOffice, and the scans by rasterising and degrading a PDF export (examples/real-corpus/build.sh). A phone photo of a crumpled page is harder than these scans.
Matching is by distinctive phrase with OCR tolerance; a reading with the right words in the wrong structure can still match.

The blind split was measured twice, never to choose a change: after the dev tuning (items read right 110/143), and after generic fixes made for failures found elsewhere — a benchmark regression on a per-glyph-bullet PDF and one held-out item lost silently (114/143). Both measurements are kept in docs/baseline/uw3c.
